registry: The Tank Guide University Research Library

verification_status.unverified_citation_from_package: Citation metadata recorded as given in the package; not yet checked against the live source.

evidence_role.reference_data: Source of specific numeric values or relationships used by the package.
evidence_role.applied_guidance: Extension/aquaculture applied guidance; context differs from home aquariums.
evidence_role.preparedness_and_safety_guidance: General emergency-preparedness or safety guidance; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.preparedness_context: Contextual background for severe-weather preparedness; not aquarium-specific.
evidence_role.analogous_guidance_limited_scope: Non-aquarium guidance used only for a narrowly stated principle.
evidence_role.manufacturer_product_documentation: Vendor documentation of its own product features. Not independent scientific evidence.

sources.title: Chapter A6.2, Dissolved Oxygen, National Field Manual for the Collection of Water-Quality Data
sources.publication_or_publisher: U.S. Geological Survey — National Field Manual for the Collection of Water-Quality Data
sources.package_description: Table 6.2-2 provides freshwater oxygen solubility by temperature and atmospheric pressure.
notes: Year not stated in the package.
Package uses Table 6.2-2 values at 760 mm Hg (8.42 mg/L at 24°C, 7.56 mg/L at 30°C) and is the stated source for Figure 1 and the tropical-tank table.

Package also cites S1 as research basis for the fan/evaporative-cooling subsection; the package's own description of S1 covers oxygen solubility only, so that relationship is recorded as cited but flagged for review in source-usage.json.

sources.title: Dissolved Oxygen and Water
sources.publication_or_publisher: U.S. Geological Survey — Water Science School
sources.package_description: Explains that cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warm water.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.

sources.title: CADDIS: Dissolved Oxygen
sources.package_description: Describes atmospheric oxygen absorption, enhancement by turbulence, and high-temperature reduction in oxygen solubility.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.
Package also relies on this source for 'fish gulping air' as a biological effect associated with low dissolved oxygen (Section 4).

sources.title: The effects of temperature on aerobic metabolism
sources.package_description: Peer-reviewed review describing temperature-metabolism relationships and thermal performance.
notes: DOI not given in the package; URL is a PubMed record, not the publisher page.
Volume, issue, and pages not given in the package.

Package uses this source to support 'aerobic metabolic rate generally rises with temperature and then can decline at higher temperatures' and explicitly rejects a universal 'metabolism doubles' claim.

sources.title: Dissolved Oxygen for Fish Production
sources.publication_or_publisher: University of Florida IFAS Extension (publication FA002, per URL)
sources.package_description: Discusses warm water holding less oxygen and increasing fish physiological oxygen demand.
notes: Year and authors not stated in the package.
Aquaculture/fish-production context; package limitations note that home aquariums are smaller systems and application should remain cautious.

sources.title: Aeration of Ponds Used in Aquaculture
sources.author_or_organization: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service / University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff
sources.publication_or_publisher: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (hosted by University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff)
sources.package_description: Describes diffusion, turbulence, and physical agitation of surface water as mechanisms of atmospheric oxygen transfer.
notes: Package attributes the document jointly to USDA-NRCS and UAPB; classified as government because the package text and file name identify it as NRCS guidance (NRCS-AEN-3). University co-attribution retained; needs verification.
Year and authors not stated in the package. The '2023/07' in the URL is the host upload path, not a confirmed publication date.
Pond aquaculture context; package cautions that home-aquarium application should remain cautious.

sources.title: CADDIS: Ammonia
sources.package_description: Explains ammonia forms, the more toxic un-ionized NH3 form, and effects of pH and temperature.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.

sources.title: Aquatic Life Ambient Water Quality Criteria for Ammonia - Freshwater 2013
sources.package_description: Includes ammonia speciation relationships, pH effects, and temperature equation.
notes: Year 2013 is taken from the document title as given in the package.
Package uses this source for the '~tenfold per pH unit, ~twofold per 10°C (0–30°C)' relationship and as the basis for its own calculated Figure 2 NH3-fraction table.
Package caveat: the Figure 2 table is 'a chemistry illustration, not a safe-exposure chart.'

sources.title: Water Quality Considerations for Aquaculture
sources.author_or_organization: Ohio State University / aquaculture water-quality guidance
sources.publication_or_publisher: Ohio State University (OSU South Centers, per URL)
sources.package_description: Notes increased fish oxygen consumption after feeding and other drivers of oxygen demand.
notes: Package attribution is itself hedged ('Ohio State University / aquaculture water-quality guidance'); authorship and original publisher need verification.
Classified university_extension because the package calls it 'Ohio State aquaculture guidance' hosted on an OSU South Centers site; needs verification.
Year not stated in the package.

sources.title: Guidelines for the Use of Fishes in Research
sources.author_or_organization: American Fisheries Society, American Institute of Fishery Research Biologists, and American Society of Ichthyologists and Herpetologists
sources.publication_or_publisher: American Fisheries Society et al. (copy hosted by UC Santa Barbara research office)
sources.package_description: States sufficient aeration can be supplied by compressed air, oxygen, or agitation.
notes: URL is a third-party institutional copy (UCSB IACUC), not the publishing societies' own site.
Research-facility context; package cautions that home-aquarium application should remain cautious.

sources.title: Guidelines on: the care and use of fish in research, teaching and testing
sources.publication_or_publisher: Canadian Council on Animal Care (copy hosted by Oregon State University research office)
sources.package_description: Recommends emergency contingency capacity, backup power, and longer-outage plans for aquatic life support.
notes: Year not stated in the package. The URL file name contains '2005', which may indicate the edition but is not confirmed by the package.
URL is a third-party institutional copy (Oregon State University IACUC), not the CCAC's own site.
Research-facility context; package cautions that home-aquarium application should remain cautious.

sources.title: Power Outages
sources.package_description: General outage preparation and generator safety guidance.
notes: Year not stated in the package. Web page; publication/update date not recorded.
Package uses it for the generator placement safety note (outdoors, at least 20 feet from building openings) and general outage preparation; not aquarium-specific.

sources.title: How to Create and Store an Emergency Water Supply
sources.author_or_organization: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.publication_or_publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.package_description: Used only for clean-container and covered-storage preparedness principles; it is not aquarium-specific guidance.
notes: Package explicitly limits this source's use: 'written for human emergency water, not aquarium husbandry.'
Year not stated in the package.

sources.title: WiFi Aquarium Temperature Controller ITC-306A (official product page)
notes: MANUFACTURER SOURCE — not independent scientific evidence. Documents the vendor's own advertised product features only.
Package: the INKBIRD recommendation is 'supportable as a brand-specific example'; features are model-specific and not every controller has Wi-Fi, alerts, dual relays, or heating-and-cooling control.
The Tank Guide article that relies on this package recommends INKBIRD by name; any commercial relationship is not recorded in the package and is not assessed here.
Product pages change without versioning; no capture date recorded in the package.

sources.title: ITC-308 Wi-Fi with Aquarium Probe (official product page)
sources.package_description: Documents model-specific heating and cooling control.
notes: MANUFACTURER SOURCE — not independent scientific evidence. Documents the vendor's own advertised product features only.
Package: features are model-specific; INKBIRD is 'a brand example, not a claim that every INKBIRD controller has the same alarms, connectivity, or outputs.'
Product pages change without versioning; no capture date recorded in the package.
